title: AVL left rotation and reattachment to the parent
summary: Perform a left rotation on unbalanced node 4, turning the right-leaning chain 4 → 5 → 6 into a balanced subtree rooted at 5 with left child 4 and right child 6.
context: The outer root of the whole tree is 1, with left child 0 and right child 4; node 4 has only right child 5, and node 5 has only right child 6. The figure labels unbalanced node 4 as node and its right child 5 as child.

A node's balance factor is its left subtree height minus its right subtree height, with leaf height 0 and empty subtree height −1; a tree is balanced only when every node's balance factor has absolute value at most 1. The balance factors below are computed from the connections shown.
description: The three subfigures show before rotation, after local rotation, and after reattachment to the parent, rather than line-by-line code assignment snapshots. Initially, node 4 has left subtree height −1 and right subtree height 1, giving balance factor −2; outer root 1 also has balance factor −2.
Left rotation raises 5 to become the local root, makes 4 its left child, and keeps 6 as its right child. Because 5 originally had no left child, 4's right child is empty after the rotation.

In the middle view, the only solid edges are 1→0, 5→4, and 5→6; no solid edge yet connects parent node 1 to new root 5. A dashed circle at node 4's former position and a dashed edge from that old position to 5 appear solely for pre-rotation comparison and do not represent an extra node or active link. Only the final subfigure draws 1→5 and removes the dashed guide.
result: The table compares all parent-child links before and after, while the inorder traversal sequence remains [0, 1, 4, 5, 6].

frames.title: AVL left rotation and reattachment to the parent
frames.explanation: Once the new subtree root is reattached, the height of parent node 1's right subtree drops from 2 to 1; its left child 0 is unchanged, restoring balance to the entire tree.

steps.title: Locate the right-leaning subtree
steps.explanation: Before rotation: outer root 1 connects to left 0 and right 4; 4 connects only to right 5, and 5 connects only to right 6, with all other branches empty. Here node=4 and child=5; 4 has left height −1 and right height 1, giving balance factor −2 and requiring a left rotation.
steps.key_state: Initially, root 1 connects to left 0 and right 4; 4 connects to right 5, and 5 connects to right 6; node 4 has balance factor −2, ready to rotate left.
steps.announcement: Identify unbalanced node 4 and its right child 5.

steps.title: Complete local rotation, awaiting reattachment
steps.explanation: After the local left rotation, the solid links split into two disconnected parts: 1 connects only to left 0, while new root 5 connects to left 4 and right 6, with both 4 and 6 as leaf nodes. Parent node 1 has no solid link to 5 yet, so the tree is not yet reconnected as a whole. The dashed circle at 4's former position and its dashed edge to 5 are only for comparison; there are still just the five nodes 0, 1, 4, 5, and 6.
steps.key_state: After local left rotation, 1 connects only to left 0; new root 5 connects to left 4 and right 6, with 1 not yet linked to 5.
steps.announcement: Local left rotation complete; not yet reattached to parent node 1.

steps.title: Reattach the new subtree root to 1
steps.explanation: Attach new root 5 as the right child of parent node 1 and remove the dashed old-position guide: root 1 now connects to left 0 and right 5; 5 connects to left 4 and right 6, with 0, 4, and 6 as leaf nodes. The height of 1's right subtree drops to 1, restoring balance across the whole tree while keeping the inorder sequence [0, 1, 4, 5, 6].
steps.key_state: After reattachment, root 1 connects to left 0 and right 5; 5 connects to left 4 and right 6, balancing the whole tree.
steps.announcement: Reattach new subtree root 5 to parent node 1, completing the left rotation.
